input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-Readiness Assessment for Llama Stack

## Description

Investigation that closes the strategy's defining unknown: no systematic
GA-readiness assessment of Llama Stack has been done, and TP feedback is
scattered across support tickets. This epic inventories the gaps between current
Tech Preview quality and the GA bar across API stability, upgrade paths, scale
limits, and error handling, and produces the definitive GA scope for the
graduation effort. Its findings determine the scope of the downstream API
stability/hardening work and the production support posture.

## Scope

- Collect and triage Tech Preview feedback from support tickets and other
  feedback channels into a single gap record.
- Assess API stability: inventory the published API surface and identify
  unstable, unversioned, or undocumented endpoints and behaviors.
- Assess upgrade paths: exercise upgrades between Tech Preview releases and
  record incompatibilities and migration friction.
- Assess scale limits: identify the operational limits of supported deployment
  shapes and where behavior under load is unknown.
- Assess error handling: identify where errors are unstructured, leaked, or
  undocumented.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: a prioritized gap inventory with
  each gap classified as GA-blocking or deferrable, forming the baseline for
  the API stability and support-posture work.
- Ratify the GA scope with product stakeholders.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gap inventory exists covering all four assessment areas (API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with each gap traceable to TP
  feedback or to systematic testing performed by this investigation.
- Every gap in the inventory is classified as GA-blocking or deferrable with a
  stated rationale.
- The definitive GA scope document is published and ratified by product
  stakeholders, and it is sufficient to re-baseline the scope and estimates of
  the downstream stability and support-posture work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): fully covered — this epic is the GA-readiness assessment that
  inventories the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar and produces
  the definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantees and TP Upgrade Path

## Description

Implements the published API surface stability guarantee for Llama Stack at GA:
versioned APIs, a documented deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from
the last two Tech Preview releases, plus the hardening needed to close
GA-blocking gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment. This epic delivers
HLR-2 and is the core code-change epic of the graduation effort.

## Scope

- Apply explicit versioning to the published API surface (the
  LlamaStackDistribution CRD and the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs), per the
  ratified GA scope.
- Define and document the API deprecation policy covering the versioned surface.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from each of the last two Tech Preview
  releases.
- Remediate the GA-blocking API stability and error-handling gaps identified by
  the GA-readiness assessment (gaps classified as deferrable in the ratified GA
  scope are explicitly out of this epic's scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published API surface carries explicit versioning, and the versioned
  surface is documented.
- A deprecation policy is documented and applies to the versioned API surface.
- Automated tests exercise the upgrade from each of the last two Tech Preview
  releases and pass.
- Every GA-blocking API stability and error-handling gap from the GA-readiness
  assessment is remediated, or its deferral is recorded with rationale in the
  ratified GA scope.
- No new feature development beyond GA-bar quality work (strategy out-of-scope
  boundary is respected).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): fully covered — versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and tested
  upgrade path from the last two TP releases.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

Establishes the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO
targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. This epic
delivers HLR-3 and turns the quality bar defined by the GA-readiness assessment
into supportable commitments.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA component.
- Define the backport policy covering GA releases and the last two Tech Preview
  releases.
- Define the supported configuration matrix (deployment shapes, provider
  combinations, and scale limits), validated against the scale-limit findings of
  the GA-readiness assessment.
- Validate the supported configuration matrix with tests or recorded evidence
  for each supported combination.
- Publish the support posture through the product's support documentation
  channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and reviewed by the owning and support
  stakeholders.
- The backport policy is documented and covers GA releases and the last two
  Tech Preview releases.
- The supported configuration matrix enumerates every supported combination,
  and each entry is backed by test evidence produced by this epic's validation
  work.
- Unsupported combinations are explicitly listed as out of support.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): fully covered — documented SLO targets, backport policy, and
  supported configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI Guardrails as a Supported Integration for GA Distributions

## Description

Promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag to a
supported, documented integration for GA distributions of Llama Stack. This
epic delivers HLR-4: at GA, customers consume guardrails as a supported
capability, not an opt-in experiment. This epic spans two components — the
TrustyAI guardrails service surfaces and the Llama Stack distribution
configuration that exposes them — with TrustyAI as the most-relevant owning
component. The integration documentation states the integration's own support
boundaries; its consistency with the platform-wide GA support posture (SLOs,
backport policy, supported configuration matrix) is verified during the GA
documentation uplift, which runs after both this epic and the support-posture
publication.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental/opt-in flag gating for the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration in GA distributions of Llama Stack.
- Validate the integration end to end against TrustyAI service deployments,
  covering the supported configuration for GA distributions.
- Document the supported integration: configuration, usage, and the
  integration's own support boundaries (supported guardrails configurations,
  and any limits narrower than the GA distribution's overall support
  commitments, stated explicitly). This published integration documentation is
  the authoritative source for the guardrails integration; the GA documentation
  uplift cross-links and uplifts it rather than re-authoring it.
- Fold any incidental updates to TrustyAI-side integration references that fall
  out of this change into this epic's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA distribution ships with the TrustyAI guardrails integration available as
  a supported capability, with no experimental flag required to enable it.
- The integration is validated end to end against TrustyAI service deployments,
  with recorded evidence covering the supported configuration.
- Documentation for the supported integration is published, including
  configuration, usage, and support boundaries.
- The documented support boundaries for the guardrails integration are stated
  explicitly — the supported guardrails configurations and any limits narrower
  than the GA distribution's overall support commitments — so that the GA
  documentation uplift can verify them against the published platform support
  posture.
- The experimental flag (or its documentation) is removed or marked deprecated
  with a migration path.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): fully covered — safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported,
  documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

# Enable Llama Stack Management in the Dashboard by Default

## Description

Removes the Tech Preview opt-in gate so that the Dashboard enables Llama Stack
management by default for entitled clusters. This epic delivers HLR-5: at GA,
entitled customers get Llama Stack management surfaces without any opt-in step.
The Dashboard's existing per-component feature flag and defaults mechanism
(OdhDashboardConfig) is the surface this change rides on.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack feature flag/defaults so that Llama Stack
  management is enabled by default on entitled clusters.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management.
- Verify that non-entitled clusters are unaffected (no Llama Stack management
  surfaces appear without entitlement).
- Fold incidental UI caption/status updates that fall out of the
  Tech-Preview-to-GA label change into this epic's scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default Dashboard configuration, Llama Stack
  management surfaces are available with no opt-in action by the user.
- The Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management is removed from the
  Dashboard code and configuration.
- On a non-entitled cluster, no Llama Stack management surfaces are exposed.
- The change is exercised by automated tests covering both entitled and
  non-entitled clusters.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): fully covered — the Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by
  default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

# Llama Stack GA Documentation Uplift and TP Migration Notes

## Description

Uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including migration notes
from Tech Preview, reflecting the GA API surface, the production support
posture, and the supported integrations that the graduation effort delivers.
This epic delivers HLR-6 and runs last: the documentation describes what was
actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- GA-standard documentation for the Llama Stack component, replacing
  Tech Preview framing and caveats.
- Documentation of the versioned API surface, deprecation policy, and the
  upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview, covering upgrade steps and behavior
  changes customers must account for.
- Uplift and cross-link the TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation
  (configuration, usage, and support boundaries) published by the guardrails
  promotion work to GA documentation standards. That published integration
  documentation is the authoritative source — it is referenced and uplifted
  here, not independently re-authored.
- Documentation of default Llama Stack management in the Dashboard for
  entitled clusters.
- Cross-links to the support posture documentation (SLO targets, backport
  policy, supported configuration matrix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation meets GA standards and no longer carries Tech Preview framing
  for the graduated capability.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview are published and cover the upgrade path
  and behavior changes from the last two TP releases.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented GA behavior
  (API surface, support posture, guardrails integration, and Dashboard
  enablement) and discrepancies found in review are corrected.
- The TrustyAI guardrails integration documentation published by the
  guardrails promotion work is uplifted to GA documentation standards and
  cross-linked from the GA documentation set (the authoritative
  configuration, usage, and support-boundary content is referenced, not
  re-authored), and documentation of default Llama Stack management in the
  Dashboard for entitled clusters is published.
- The documented TrustyAI guardrails support boundaries are verified against
  the published GA support posture for Llama Stack distributions (SLO
  targets, backport policy, supported configuration matrix): where the
  guardrails integration is narrower than the platform posture, the narrower
  boundary is stated explicitly; no documented guardrails boundary exceeds
  the platform posture; and discrepancies found are corrected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-6 (P2): fully covered — documentation is uplifted to GA standards,
  including migration notes from TP.
